findings.obligation: Non-blocking. RED completeness: each defect fails naming it (acceptance S3 falsifier, E3/E6)
findings.observation: ThenEveryVerdictPasses calls verdict.Check() in a foreach, and Check throws on the first failing verdict. The RED for test 1 names only the Platform.UsageData group (PlatformUsageLoggingReleasesLayoutArchUnitTest.cs:61) and test 2 only the UsageData test classes (:69). The Logging and Releases verdicts are never evaluated in RED. Evidence: R1.
findings.remediation: Collect every verdict failure into one list and assert it is empty, so all areas name their defects in one RED run. Not a veto: the falsifier still fails for a Logging or Releases defect.

findings.obligation: Non-blocking. Expected: every type resolves to exactly one type in Platform.<area>; a second copy is a falsifier (acceptance S3 wording)
findings.observation: Exactly-one is never counted. TypesLiveInTheirLayer (ModuleRules.cs:150) checks GetType on the new full name and simple-name hits in the old namespaces. Exactly-one holds only by IL uniqueness within one assembly. A copy placed in another Platform area, or in the test assembly, is not a falsifier the oracle lists. Evidence: R3.
findings.remediation: Either state in the Expected text that exactly-one is the IL uniqueness of GetType, or count matching simple names across the production assembly and assert the count is one. Not a veto.

findings.obligation: Non-blocking. Expected: UsageDataEventName gains no member (P3: no UsageDataEventName added)
findings.observation: The Expected text of the public oracle states that UsageDataEventName gains no member. No assertion in the five tests reads UsageDataEventName. The P3 event-equality part is carried by the platform-answers-compare probe (usage-data state) in acceptance E3, not by this oracle.
findings.remediation: Either add a finite member-count check on UsageDataEventName against the value at the slice base, or name platform-answers-compare as the observation that discharges this clause. Not a veto.
